objective: Define the smallest user-facing hybrid entrypoint surface that moves the existing sidecar flow toward a future Verilator-like option without claiming Verilator-native implementation.

deferred_inputs.reason: The current reproducible source boundary is still tracked slice-launch templates generated from target/top/overlay metadata. A raw filelist can become a first-class operator input only after a later gate defines how top module, clock/reset, overlay, coverage manifest, acceptance policy, and output report paths are derived without hidden local assumptions.
Template paths remain the reproducible source-of-truth execution form. Target names are the shortest operator-facing Verilator-like surface and must resolve to tracked templates before execution.

shape_policy.reason: Existing evidence consistently favors many-state single-launch shapes over single-state repeated-step shapes, but automatic optimum selection is not yet proven for arbitrary designs.

required_visibility: dry-run must print the delegated command plan before execution
preflight and operator-plan JSON must expose target, shape, template, stage commands, correctness policy, and non-claims
efficiency estimates must remain estimates separate from correctness
coverage_output_equivalence remains the accepted CPU-vs-hybrid comparison policy
not_yet_automatic: resident execution handoff through a direct Verilator option

required_next_gate.name: run_verilator_like_hybrid_entrypoint_option_surface_dry_run_gate
must_record: all dry-run and inspection commands exit 0
operator-facing commands use target name plus --sim-accel-shape
operator-plan JSON exposes the delegated stage plan
printed Verilator command remains a synthesized handoff preview
the preview includes coverage_output_equivalence and generated report paths
the result does not claim Verilator has a native --sim-accel implementation

non_claims: not a runtime or ABI change
not a raw filelist ingestion implementation
not automatic optimal GPU assignment for any design
